editorial.headline: Processed-Meat Retail: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This specialised processed-meat retail activity permits 100% foreign ownership nationally, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium makes registration there unavailable.
editorial.body:
**This is a retail activity defined by processed meat.** The scope is specialised retail sale of varied processed-meat products, not a broad food-trade label. Its examples—sausages, bakso meatballs, and abon, a shredded-meat preparation—make the commercial centre of gravity clear: the sale of meat that has already been prepared or processed. The scope spans products made from beef, pork, poultry, lamb, rabbit, goat and camel, as well as other fresh meats named in the record. The record presents a retail activity whose identity comes from the processed nature of its merchandise. That specificity keeps the registration anchored to a particular retail offer rather than to meat in general.

**The scale range is broad.** The activity is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scale. That is the whole stated scale spectrum, so it is not presented as a narrow category available only to one business size. The scope remains specialised retail of processed-meat products of the kinds described in the record. For operators, this produces a clear description: a specialty retail business centred on processed-meat goods. The four scale labels set out the stated business-size range; they do not broaden the activity into meat commerce generally. Its boundaries remain merchandise-led and retail-specific.

**Nationally, the foreign-investment position is direct.** The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain terms, the national setting allows full foreign ownership for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no need to soften that national reading: 100% is the ceiling supplied by the record, and it sits alongside access for the four listed business scales. For founders considering the activity at a national level, this is an open PMA position, expressed without a lower foreign-ownership cap in the supplied data.

**Bali changes the conclusion completely.** Although nationally open, this activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali. Its Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO because, at Besar scale, OSS risk is recorded as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah for every scope. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA; the record ties this outcome to the moratorium of 13 May 2026. The operational answer is therefore plain: a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. National permission to hold up to 100% does not override the Bali block. The distinction is not a technical footnote; it is the decisive fact for a Bali-based foreign-owned proposal.
editorial.pullQuote: National permission to hold up to 100% does not override the Bali block.
